name: Tessera TK-11 Specter 'Whisper'
description:
The Tessera TK-11 Specter is an integrally suppressed semi-automatic pistol chambered in .45 ACP subsonic, designed from the ground up as a quiet weapon rather than a conventional pistol with a suppressor attached. The barrel and suppressor are a single monolithic unit — there is no thread, no attachment point, no way to separate the two without destroying the weapon. This integrated design reduces the overall length compared to a pistol-plus-suppressor combination and eliminates the point-of-impact shift that threaded suppressors can introduce.

The Specter is quiet. Not movie-quiet — there is still a mechanical clack from the action cycling and a muted thump from the subsonic round breaking the air — but quiet enough that the sound does not carry beyond twenty meters in an urban environment with ambient noise. Combined with the .45 ACP's inherent subsonic velocity, the weapon produces no supersonic crack, making it extraordinarily difficult to locate by sound alone.

Tessera developed the Specter under a classified corponation internal security contract and subsequently released a commercial version with identical performance. The message was clear: what Tessera uses to protect its own interests, it is willing to sell to those who can afford it. The commercial Specter costs as much as a mid-range vehicle.
specifications:
caliber: .45 ACP subsonic
effective_range: 35 meters
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 10 rounds
weight: 1.05 kg
sound_signature: <75dB at 1 meter
tactical_use: A purpose-built quiet weapon for operations requiring minimal sound signature. The integral suppressor provides consistent performance without the drawbacks of detachable suppressors. Effective at close range against unarmored targets. The subsonic .45 ACP round sacrifices velocity for silence, reducing effectiveness against body armor. Best employed in environments where sound discipline is paramount.
cultural_context: The Whisper occupies a morally ambiguous space in GLMZ's weapons culture. Owning one is legal with proper licensing, but it marks the owner as someone who has specifically planned for situations requiring silence — which implies premeditation. Law enforcement and corponation security view Specter owners with heightened scrutiny.
story_hooks: A series of silent killings in the Mids all trace to .45 ACP subsonic rounds — but the ballistic signatures come from three different Specters, all registered to the same corporate shell company.

A Tessera engineer who worked on the Specter program is selling design documents that reveal the weapon has a hidden acoustic signature — a frequency fingerprint that Tessera can use to identify every shot fired by every Specter ever manufactured.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, brutalist pistol with a distinctly forward-heavy profile. The monolithic barrel-suppressor dominates the weapon's silhouette, creating a tapered cone that extends nearly a third of the overall length. The slide sits recessed above this integrated suppressor, giving the weapon an almost organic, predatory appearance—like something designed to slip through shadows rather than command attention.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 22.5 cm | Slide length: 14.8 cm | Suppressor section: 9.2 cm | Grip height: 12.1 cm | Width at frame: 3.4 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced. The 1.05 kg mass is distributed forward into the monolithic suppressor unit, creating a slight muzzle-heavy feel that actually aids control during the minimal recoil of subsonic fire. Settles in the hand with deliberate, purposeful weight.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade aluminum alloy frame with hardened steel slide. The monolithic barrel-suppressor is hammer-forged steel with internal baffling. Trigger assembly uses titanium components to minimize wear.
physical_description.finish: Matte black DLC (diamond-like carbon) coating on all steel surfaces—non-reflective, slightly textured, designed to defeat optical targeting. The aluminum frame has a darker gunmetal anodize that resists fingerprints and corrosion. All edges are beveled and dehorned.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal black primary with gunmetal gray accents. Suppressor cone features faint machining marks that catch light only at specific angles. No contrasting colors or chrome—pure utilitarian darkness.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressively textured polymer with shallow crosshatching. Not rubberized—intentionally rough to maintain control even with wet or gloved hands. The backstrap has subtle ridging that guides the thumb naturally to the safety.
distinctive_features: Monolithic barrel-suppressor as integral single unit with visible baffle stack geometry
Recessed, low-profile slide with serrated rear sight notch only—no front sight post to catch light
Ambidextrous thumb safety with barely perceptible detents
Magazine well is slightly beveled for one-handed reloads in darkness
Trigger guard is slightly oversize to accommodate gloved operation
Minimal muzzle flash signature visible as faint signature marks on the suppressor exit
Custom internal lightening cuts visible through ejection port
No safety takedown lever—fieldstrip requires specialized tool to prevent casual disassembly
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA TK-11 SPECTER stamped in tiny serif font on the slide's left side, barely visible in direct light. Serial number engraved on the frame interior only, inaccessible without disassembly. A small Tessera corporate logo (stylized 'T' within a circle) laser-etched on the dust cover, also subdued.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-new examples are mirror-finished within the matte coating. Field-used Spectres show wear primarily on the grip texture, suppressor baffles (from gases), and trigger guard. Holster marks are common on the frame. Unlike most pistols, the suppressor rarely shows external damage—the integrated design protects it. Professional operators maintain these meticulously; they cost as much as used groundcars.
